findings.text: Registration routine for dynamically allocated lock class keys rejects statically allocated objects, selects a hash bucket from the key address, and inserts at the head for concurrent readers while holding graph serialization with interrupts saved. It guards against duplicate insertion and counts successful registrations.

Provides lookup or create semantics for lock classes keyed by map key and subclass, with validation of key origin, allocation from a free pool into global hash and list structures, recording of naming and type attributes, subclass aware caching, and rejection on subclass mismatch or allocation failure. Callers must have interrupts disabled and creation is serialized.

Every lock class is required to live in one membership place among the global list, the free list, or a delayed zap list, and every forward and backward dependency list attached to a class must contain only entries whose target back reference equals the owning class, with diagnostics emitted on violation.

Each stored chain carries a key that must equal the result of iteratively combining an initial value with the sequence of held lock identifiers spanning base and depth. Mismatch indicates corruption and is reported with chain position and expected versus recomputed values, while builds without proving support accept unconditionally.

Usage bookkeeping and linkage must agree: entries marked in use must be reachable from some class forward or backward list, and entries marked free must be absent from all such lists. Violations are reported with entry position and associated class names.

Global lock tracking structures initialize at most once with separate completion flags for general data and for deferred free handling. Deferred handling becomes ready only after scheduling is available, while general initialization prepares zap lists, moves all classes to the free pool, clears dependency lists, and prepares chain storage. Repeated calls have no further effect. An alternate build provides empty bucket preparation with no effect.

Breadth search uses a fixed capacity queue holding pointers to dependency entries plus front and rear positions. A single global instance backs all searches, accompanied by a high water mark for observed depth and a monotonically increased search generation counter.

Queue emptiness holds when front and rear coincide, fullness when the wrapped successor of rear meets front, and occupancy is the wrapped difference. Enqueue stores at rear then advances, dequeue returns from front then advances, and initialization resets both positions and advances the search generation.

Search visitation is recorded per class using the current generation identifier rather than clearing state, and dependency entries carry parent links forming a path back to the root. Depth is the number of parent hops to the root, and sibling iteration proceeds through the parent dependency list.

Dependency search explores class relationships either forward or backward from a root, applying caller supplied skip and match predicates to reachable entries. It suppresses weak paths using read mode derived strength, records the first matching entry, tracks peak queue occupancy, and reports distinct outcomes for match, no match, queue exhaustion, and invalid nodes. Forward and backward variants differ only in which dependency direction is traversed.

Strength of an ordering edge between two held locks is encoded in four possibilities derived from exclusive versus shared versus recursive read modes of predecessor and successor, with separate forward and backward encodings. Traversal propagates a flag indicating whether only weak read like edges have been seen and discards extensions that cannot form a strong path.

The strong read position is zero, the exclusive read position is one, the strong non read position is two, and the exclusive non read position is three, with each corresponding mask selecting only its own position.
Search outcomes are encoded as negative two for invalid node, negative one for queue full, zero for match found, and one for no match, with negative values classified as errors.
Queue capacity is two raised to a configurable bit count, and the index mask is one less than that capacity, providing power of two wraparound for front and rear arithmetic.

Variable length chain storage is managed in size indexed buckets with oversize blocks kept separately in decreasing size order and fixed sizes kept as unsorted stacks. Allocation size maps to bucket by subtracting one except oversize which uses bucket zero, freed space updates free totals and large block counts, and requests smaller than two cannot be represented and are accounted as lost.

Free chain blocks are threaded directly inside the held lock identifier array using leading cells for linkage with a distinguishing flag and, for oversize blocks, trailing cells for size split across two halves. Initialization marks all buckets empty then offers the whole array as one free block.

Mutation of classes, dependency lists, key hashes, and chain structures serializes under the graph lock with interrupts disabled, while hash and dependency iteration relies on read side protection without that lock. Registration saves and restores interrupt state around serialization, allocation expects disabled interrupts, and statistics updates require disabled interrupts in checking builds but vanish otherwise.

Exhaustion of classes, dependency entries, or search queue space disables further checking and emits diagnostics with stack context under emergency console protection. Singleton chain fragments are deliberately leaked and counted, duplicate key registration warns once, and hash collisions with mismatched subclass are rejected.

Static keys are never treated as dynamic and trigger a once only warning when presented as such. When checking is disabled, dynamic status is assumed true to avoid touching possibly freed hash state; otherwise membership is determined by hash lookup under read side protection.
The dependency list for an entry is obtained by applying a byte displacement to its class base, with forward search using the after displacement and backward search using the before displacement.
Full structural validation runs at most once and only when an explicit consistency flag is enabled, warning once on failure. An alternate build provides an empty validation routine with no effect.
Circular dependency reporting is suppressed entirely under silent mode; otherwise it prints call depth, class identity, and the associated saved stack with fixed indentation.

Dependency entries are allocated by scanning for the first clear usage bit and marking it used with a global count, and insertion records owning class, target class, strength, distance, and trace before appending with concurrency safe linkage. Allocation and removal occur under graph serialization while traversal uses read side protection.
Key buckets are selected by hashing the key address with a fixed bit width to index the global key table.
